chunks.l2:
[tal-a33-v00] Now the unification, arrived in due course, is discussed.

[tal-a33-v01] Since it was said the triad is to be worshipped together with the cakra-divisions: here, in this manner, is their unification.

[tal-a33-v10] Arghīśa and Bhārabhūti, Sthiti, Sthāṇu, Hara, thus; Jhaṇṭi, Bhautika, Sadyoja, Anugraha, Krūra, Sainika.

[tal-a33-v02] Viśvā, her Mistress, Hāraudrī, Vīranetrī, Ambikā, and Gurvī, thus: the goddesses shown in the Siddhāvīra, in the six-spoked wheel.

[tal-a33-v03] Māheśī, Brāhmaṇī, Skāndī, Vaiṣṇavī, Aindrī, Yamātmikā, Cāmuṇḍā indeed, and Yogīśī — thus eight, or the Aghorī-group and the rest.

[tal-a33-v04] Joined with the twelve — the mothers of Fire, Nirṛti, Wind, and Īśa: Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Kālī, Karālī, Vikṛtānanā.

[tal-a33-v05] Kroṣṭukī and Bhīmamudrā, Vāyuvegā, Hayānanā, Gambhīrā, and Ghoṣaṇī, thus: the rule in the twenty-four-spoked wheel.

[tal-a33-v06] Siddhi, Vṛddhi, Dyuti, Lakṣmī, Medhā, Kānti, Sudhā, Dhṛti, Dīpti, Puṣṭi, Mati, Kīrti, Susthiti, Sugati, Smṛti.

[tal-a33-v07] Suprabhā — sixteen in all, thus: the Śrīkaṇṭha-headed powers. Bali and Balinanda, Daśagrīva, Hara, Haya.

[tal-a33-v08] Mādhava in the six-spoked wheel; but in the twelve-spoked these are remembered: Dakṣa, Caṇḍa, Hara, Śauṇḍī, Pramatha, Bhīma and Manmatha.

[tal-a33-v09] Śakuni, Sumati, Nanda, Gopāla and Pitāmaha; Śrīkaṇṭha, Ananta, Sūkṣma, and Trimūrti, Śaṃbareśvara.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-:C33 atha śrītantrāloke trayastriṃśamāhnikam athāvasarasaṃprāpta ekīkāro nigadyate / 0b yaduktaṃ cakrabhedena sārdhaṃ pūjyamiti trikam / tatraiṣa cakrabhedānāmekīkāro diśānayā viśvā tadīśā hāraudrī vīranetryambikā tathā / gurvīti ṣaḍare devyaḥ śrīsiddhāvīradarśitāḥ māheśī brāhmaṇī skāndī vaiṣṇavyaindrī yamātmikā / cāmuṇḍā caiva yogīśītyaṣṭāghoryādayo@thavā agninirṛtivāyvīśamātṛbhirdvādaśānvitāḥ / nandā bhadrā jayā kālī karālī vikṛtānanā kroṣṭukī bhīmamudrā ca vāyuvegā hayānanā / gambhīrā ghoṣaṇī ceti caturviṃśatyare vidhiḥ siddhirvṛddhirdyutirlakṣmīrmedhā kāntiḥ sudhā dhṛtiḥ / dīptiḥ puṣṭirmatiḥ kīrtiḥ susthitiḥ sugatiḥ smṛtiḥ suprabhā ṣoḍaśī ceti śrīkaṇṭhādikaśaktayaḥ / baliśca balinandaśca daśagrīvo haro hayaḥ mādhavaḥ ṣaḍare cakre dvādaśāre tvamī smṛtāḥ / dakṣaścaṇḍo haraḥ śauṇḍī pramatho bhīmamanmathau śakuniḥ sumatirnando gopālaśca pitāmahaḥ / śrīkaṇṭho@nantasūkṣmau ca trimūrtiḥ śaṃbareśvaraḥ arghīśo bhārabhūtiśca sthitiḥ sthāṇurharastathā / jhaṇṭhibhautikasadyojānugrahakrūrasainikāḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a33-v11] Two-eight; whatever nectar, joined therewith: Pūrṇa, Ābha and their fluids, Ogha, Ūrmi, Syandana, Aṅga, and Vapus, Udgāra, Vaktraka.

[tal-a33-v12] Tanu, Secana, Mūrti, Īśa; Sarvāmṛtadhara, and the other; by feminine reading these powers are declared sixteen indeed.

[tal-a33-v13] Saṃvarta, Lakulī, Bhṛgu, Sita, Baka, Khaṅgī, Pinākī, Bhujaga, Bali, Kāla; Dvi and Chagalāṇḍa; Śikhī, Śoṇa, Meṣa, Mīna, Tridaṇḍī; with Āṣāḍhī.

[tal-a33-v14] Devīkānta and his half; Dāruka, Hali, Somanātha, Śarman; Jaya, Vijaya, Jayantā, Jita, Sujaya, Jaya, the Rudrakīrtana-bringers.

[tal-a33-v15] Increasing zeal for His form; and the Bala, Subala, Bhadra gift-bearers; its bearer and giver, and the Lord, joyous, equal, blessed of His form.

[tal-a33-v16] Desiring well-minded Śiva-giving; Durga, time called Bhadra, mind-following Kauśika, Kāla, Viśva, Suśivās and others likewise; Kopa.

[tal-a33-v17] On the ear-fire spoke these would be; by feminine reading these are śaktis. 'Juṃkāra' and 'Agnipatnī', thus, in the six-spoked, eunuch-excluded.

[tal-a33-v18] In the twelve-spoked, those along with them; in the sixteen-spoked, the vowels in order; ha in the twice-eight-spoked; from ya to the ha-end, but, in the trika.

[tal-a33-v19] On the thirty-two-spoked, with end, bindu on the head of all; thus many other cakra-divisions one should construct from this.

[tal-a33-v20] One alone is this consciousness-self, the essence of universe-awareness; śakti and her possessor thence — mother, mass of sound — are declared a pair.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-dvyaṣṭau yadvāmṛtastena yuktāḥ pūrṇābhataddravāḥ / oghormisyandanāṅgāśca vapurudgāravaktrakāḥ tanusecanamūrtīśāḥ sarvāmṛtadharo@paraḥ / śrīpāṭhācchaktayaścaitāḥ ṣoḍaśaiva prakīrtitāḥ saṃvartalakulibhṛgusitabakakhaṅgipinākibhujagabalikālāḥ / dviśchagalāṇḍau śikhiśoṇameṣamīnatridaṇḍi sāṣāḍhi devīkāntatadardhau dārukahalisomanāthaśarmāṇaḥ / jayavijayajayantājitasujayajayarudrakīrtanāvahakāḥ tanmūrtyutsāhadavardhanāśca balasubalabhadradāvahakāḥ / tadvāndātā ceśo nandanasamabhadratanmūrtiḥ śivadasumanaḥspṛhaṇakā durgo bhadrākhyakālaśca / ceto@nugakauśikakālaviśvasuśivāstathāparaḥ kopaḥ śrutyagnyare syurete strīpāṭhācchaktayastvetāḥ / juṃkāro@thāgnipatnīti ṣaḍare ṣaṇṭhavarjitāḥ dvādaśāre tatsahitāḥ ṣoḍaśāre svarāḥ kramāt / halastaddviguṇe@ṣṭāre yādyaṃ hāntaṃ tu tattrike dvātriṃśadarake sāntaṃ binduḥ sarveṣu mūrdhani / evamanyānbahūṃścakrabhedānasmātprakalpayet eka eva cidātmaiṣa viśvāmarśanasārakaḥ / śaktistadvānato mātā śabdarāśiḥ prakīrtitau

chunks.l2:
[tal-a33-v21] But in the division of those two, in the fashioning of śakti and her possessor: the sound-mass and Mālinī, of agitation-nature, such a body.

[tal-a33-v22] Thus in the splitting of inner awareness, really the triad called Anuttara, Icchā, Unmeṣa — from which the universe is awareness.

[tal-a33-v23] But in union with Ānanda, Īśa, Ūrmi, that is declared the hexad; through semivowel-sibilant union that is declared the octad.

[tal-a33-v24] Then, in the absence of the four amṛta-vowels, it would be a dodecad; in union with them, called sixteen — thus until innumerability.

[tal-a33-v25] Since it clearly bears the universe from single-awareness-bearing on, bearing part-of-part awarenesses at the end.

[tal-a33-v26] Hence the fifty's oneness, vowel-manifest-variety, eight vargas, letter-division, eighty-one kalā-rise.

[tal-a33-v27] Thus shown before, from half-mora-bearing; for even vowel-half exists, of the svarita a half-mora.

[tal-a33-v28] From its beginning the udātta, that said by the pada-knower; thus this consciousness, of sacrificand-form-awareness-nature.

[tal-a33-v29] Unbroken from consciousness, this wheel-horizon of wheels; by lordship-and-veil division employ it manifoldly.

[tal-a33-v30] Parāparā, Parā, and the other: creation, maintenance, concealment; but the fourth, Mātṛsadbhāva-formed, is called repose.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tayoreva vibhāge tu śaktitadvatprakalpane / śabdarāśirmālinī ca kṣobhātma vapurīdṛśam tathāntaḥsthaparāmarśabhedane vastutastrikam / anuttarecchonmeṣākhyaṃ yato viśvaṃ vimarśanam ānandeśormiyoge tu tatṣaṭkaṃ samudāhṛtam / antaḥsthoṣmasamāyogāttadaṣṭakamudāhṛtam tadāmṛtacatuṣkonabhāve dvādaśakaṃ bhavet / tadyoge ṣoḍaśākhyaṃ syādevaṃ yāvadasaṃkhyatā viśvamekaparāmarśasahatvātprabhṛti sphuṭam / aṃśāṃśikāparāmarśān paryante sahate yataḥ ataḥ pañcāśadaikātmyaṃ svaravyaktivirūpatā / vargāṣṭakaṃ varṇabheda ekāśītikalodayaḥ iti pradarśitaṃ pūrvam ardhamātrāsahatvataḥ / svarārdhamapyasti yataḥ svaritasyārdhamātrakam tasyādita udāttaṃ tatkathitaṃ padavedinā / itthaṃ saṃvidiyaṃ yājyasvarūpāmarśarūpiṇī abhinnaṃ saṃvidaścaitaccakrāṇāṃ cakravālakam / svāmyāvaraṇabhedena bahudhā tatprayojayet parāparā parā cānyā sṛṣṭisthititirodhayaḥ / mātṛsadbhāvarūpā tu turyā viśrāntirucyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a33-v31] And that clearly mouth-seated, hinted at each word; in the Fourth, repose is to be placed, moving in Mātṛsadbhāva.

[tal-a33-v32] So to him the universe shines, gone to identity with his own self; thus told is this unification of the scripture's matter, uttered by the guru.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tacca prakāśaṃ vaktrasthaṃ sūcitaṃ tu pade pade / turye viśrāntirādheyā mātṛsadbhāvasāriṇi tathāsya viśvamābhāti svātmatanmayatāṃ gatam / ityeṣa śāstrārthasyokta ekīkāro gurūditaḥ
